description: Splits a polyphonic cable into sixteen separate outputs, and will sort the channels by voltage on the way, on its own or in step with other sorting modules

params.text: Sorts the channels from low voltage to high before they are handed out; the button latches and its lamp is lit while sorting is on

inputs.text: The polyphonic cable to split; its channel count sets how many channels the link output carries
With a cable here the sorting is done on these voltages rather than on the input's own, which is how several modules are kept in the same order; a channel reading exactly 0V is left where it is

outputs.text: One channel of the input; with sorting on, the first jack carries the lowest voltage and the last the highest
Carries the voltages the sorting was done on, so another SplitSort, MergeSort or one of these chained after it sorts into the same order

notes: the sort button does nothing to the link output's own ordering: the link output carries the unsorted voltages, and it is the module downstream that sorts by them
these can be daisy-chained, link output to link input, and the first module in the chain sets the order for all of them
this is a reimplementation of Aria Salvatrice's Splort

inputs.1:
polyphonic

unpatched it reads the input's own voltages.
